records.label: spacr.qt.gui_scale.mend_matplotlib_icons#1
records.source: Matplotlib's toolbar icon engine multiplies the size Qt asks for by the device pixel ratio, and Qt has already done so; above 1 the two cancel, below 1 (a user's ``QT_SCALE_FACTOR`` under 1) they compound. Measured offscreen at a ratio of 0.5: the icons drew 3 px tall instead of 11. Holding the engine's ratio at 1 or more draws them 11 px tall and changes nothing at a ratio of 1 or 2. Idempotent.
records.context: Matplotlib's toolbar icon engine multiplies the size Qt asks for by the device pixel ratio, and Qt has already done so; above 1 the two cancel, below 1 (a user's ``QT_SCALE_FACTOR`` under 1) they compound. Measured offscreen at a ratio of 0.5: the icons drew 3 px tall instead of 11. Holding the engine's ratio at 1 or more draws them 11 px tall and changes nothing at a ratio of 1 or 2. Idempotent.
records.translation: Matplotlib का टूलबार आइकन इंजन Qt द्वारा माँगे गए आकार को डिवाइस पिक्सेल अनुपात से गुणा करता है, और Qt पहले ही ऐसा कर चुका होता है; 1 से ऊपर दोनों एक-दूसरे को निरस्त करते हैं, 1 से नीचे (उपयोगकर्ता का ``QT_SCALE_FACTOR`` 1 से कम) वे संचयी हो जाते हैं। 0.5 अनुपात पर ऑफ़स्क्रीन मापा गया: आइकन 11 के बजाय 3 px ऊँचे बने। इंजन का अनुपात 1 या अधिक पर रखने से वे 11 px ऊँचे बनते हैं और 1 या 2 अनुपात पर कुछ नहीं बदलता। आइडेम्पोटेंट।
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.qt.help_index#11

records.label: spacr.qt.help_index.setting_entries#1
records.source: ONE ROW PER MODULE: a setting in four modules is four rows, each naming its module and the category it sits under, rather than one row that then asks which. The user already knows which module they meant; a row that asks is a second click for information the list could have shown.

records.label: spacr.qt.help_index.setting_entries#2
records.source: THE API HALF OF A SETTING IS NOT EMITTED HERE. ``SETTING_CONSUMERS`` names every addressable function that reads a key, and :func:`api_entries` folds that into the API row for each of those functions -- one row per symbol, saying which settings it reads. Emitting them from both providers listed ``spacr.io.preprocess_img_data`` once for itself and once for every setting it reads, which was eleven identical rows in one result list.
records.context: The API half of a setting is not emitted here. ``SETTING_CONSUMERS`` names every addressable function that reads a structured-data name, and :func:`api_entries` folds that into the API row for each of those functions -- one row per symbol, saying which settings it reads. Emitting them from both providers listed ``spacr.io.preprocess_img_data`` once for itself and once for every setting it reads, which was eleven identical rows in one result list.
records.translation: सेटिंग का API वाला आधा भाग यहाँ नहीं निकाला जाता। ``SETTING_CONSUMERS`` किसी कुंजी को पढ़ने वाले हर पहुँच योग्य फ़ंक्शन का नाम देता है, और :func:`api_entries` इसे उनमें से हर फ़ंक्शन की API पंक्ति में शामिल करता है -- प्रति प्रतीक एक पंक्ति, जो बताती है कि वह कौन-सी सेटिंग्स पढ़ता है। दोनों प्रदाताओं से इन्हें निकालने पर ``spacr.io.preprocess_img_data`` एक बार स्वयं के लिए और हर पढ़ी गई सेटिंग के लिए एक बार सूचीबद्ध होता था, यानी एक परिणाम सूची में ग्यारह एक जैसी पंक्तियाँ।

records.label: spacr.qt.help_search#8
records.source: NOTHING THIS MODULE DOES ON THE GUI THREAD BLOCKS IT. The index costs about a second to build, so it is built on a worker the first time the field is typed in (:class:`_IndexLoader`), and the field says so until it lands. Whether the documentation site answers is a network question, so it is asked on a worker too (:class:`_DocsReach`) and only ever when the user has opened an API result -- spaCR does not reach the network because somebody typed.
records.context: Nothing this module does on the main GUI execution path blocks it. The index costs about a second to build, so it is built on a worker the first time the field is typed in (:class:`_IndexLoader`), and the field says so until it lands. Whether the documentation site answers is a network question, so it is asked on a worker too (:class:`_DocsReach`) and only ever when the user has opened an API result -- spaCR does not reach the network because somebody typed.
records.translation: यह मॉड्यूल GUI थ्रेड पर जो कुछ करता है वह उसे कभी नहीं रोकता। इंडेक्स बनाने में लगभग एक सेकंड लगता है, इसलिए फ़ील्ड में पहली बार टाइप होने पर इसे वर्कर पर बनाया जाता है (:class:`_IndexLoader`), और बनने तक फ़ील्ड यह बताता है। दस्तावेज़ साइट उत्तर देती है या नहीं, यह नेटवर्क का प्रश्न है, इसलिए यह भी वर्कर पर पूछा जाता है (:class:`_DocsReach`) और केवल तब जब उपयोगकर्ता ने API परिणाम खोला हो -- spaCR केवल इसलिए नेटवर्क तक नहीं पहुँचता कि किसी ने टाइप किया।

records.label: spacr.qt.live_zoom#8
records.source: AND THE ICONS DID NOT MOVE AT ALL, which was NOT part of that compromise. The spacing caught up at the settle; the icons never caught up, because an icon size is neither a stylesheet value nor a ``scaled_px`` call that anything re-ran -- it is a widget PROPERTY written once when the widget was built, so a scale that grew every caption left every glyph beside those captions exactly where it was. The settle now re-derives them, through :func:`spacr.qt.preferences._rescale_icon_sizes`, inside the same ``apply_preferences_to_app`` step that rebuilds the sheet: 5.5 ms for the 2,122 widgets of a window with two modules open, against the 395-877 ms that step costs when the scale really changes. Nothing was added to the live half.

records.label: spacr.qt.live_zoom.LiveZoomFilter.settle#2
records.source: THE ICONS CATCH UP HERE TOO, and here only. They ride inside ``apply_preferences_to_app`` rather than being resized per notch, because the condition on this gesture was that it be fast without lag and the live half is the half that has to answer for it. The sweep is 5.5 ms on 2,122 widgets, so it COULD have gone in the live half -- it is here because the icons would then have grown inside spacing that had not, which is the mismatch that made the icons look wrong in the first place.

SEEDED by the dataset key, so the draw is the same on every machine: a sample that changes between two people's machines is a sample nobody can talk about -- "the third field looks wrong" has to mean the same field for both of them. A dataset with a quota draws that way within each domain.
records.context: Which fields. A random draw in which every field of the dataset has the same chance -- the first N by name are the first laboratory microplate of the first domain, which is not the dataset. SEEDED by the dataset structured-data name, so the draw is the same on every machine: a sample that changes between two people's machines is a sample nobody can talk about -- "the third field looks wrong" has to mean the same field for both of them. records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine#2
records.source: THREE INVERSIONS LIVE HERE AND THEY DO DIFFERENT THINGS (items 435 and 419 point 9). :func:`invert_intensity` is the photographic complement of an IMAGE -- ``dtype_max - value``, what a viewer's Invert does, exactly reversible on every integer dtype -- and it is what the Make Masks screen's "Invert image" draws with. :func:`invert_for_detection` reflects an image about its OWN range instead, and is what the screen's "Invert for detection" hands the detectors; its docstring has the measurement that says why a detector cannot use the complement, and it is NOT a duplicate to be merged away. :func:`invert_mask` flips a LABEL image's foreground and background; on an ordinary field that gives one object covering the frame, which is why it was reported as doing nothing.
records.context: Three inversions live here and they do different things (items 435 and 419 point 9). :func:`invert_intensity` is the photographic complement of an IMAGE -- ``dtype_max - value``, what a viewer's Invert does, exactly reversible on every integer dtype -- and it is what the Make Masks screen's "Invert image" draws with. :func:`invert_for_detection` reflects an image about its OWN range instead, and is what the screen's "Invert for detection" hands the detectors; its docstring has the measurement that says why a detector cannot use the complement, and it is NOT a duplicate to be merged away. :func:`invert_mask` flips a LABEL image's foreground and background; on an ordinary microscope field of view that gives one object covering the frame, which is why it was reported as doing nothing.
records.translation: यहाँ तीन उलटाव हैं और वे अलग-अलग काम करते हैं (आइटम 435 और 419 बिंदु 9)। :func:`invert_intensity` किसी छवि का फ़ोटोग्राफ़िक पूरक है -- ``dtype_max - value``, जो किसी व्यूअर का Invert करता है, हर पूर्णांक dtype पर ठीक-ठीक उलटा जा सकने वाला -- और Make Masks पेज का "Invert image" इसी से बनाता है। :func:`invert_for_detection` इसके बजाय छवि को उसकी अपनी सीमा के सापेक्ष परावर्तित करता है, और पेज का "Invert for detection" डिटेक्टरों को यही देता है; इसके docstring में वह माप है जो बताता है कि डिटेक्टर पूरक का उपयोग क्यों नहीं कर सकता, और यह मिलाकर हटाया जाने वाला डुप्लिकेट नहीं है। :func:`invert_mask` किसी लेबल छवि की अग्रभूमि और पृष्ठभूमि उलटता है; सामान्य फ़ील्ड पर इससे पूरे फ़्रेम को ढकने वाला एक ऑब्जेक्ट बनता है, इसीलिए इसकी रिपोर्ट कुछ न करने के रूप में हुई थी।

records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine#8
records.source: In place is sound for both, which is why there is no convert step. A sibling set differs from a nested one only in where its masks folder is, so passing that folder is the whole change. A bundle is rewritten with every key it already had kept, ``masks`` replaced, and the two keys derived from the masks -- ``outlines`` and ``ismanual`` -- brought up to date with it (see :func:`save_seg_bundle`); that is what the external curation tool did to the same files, less its stale outlines. A convert step would have been a second copy of every field, and the curator would have had to remember which copy was the truth.
records.context: In place is sound for both, which is why there is no convert step. A sibling set differs from a nested one only in where its masks folder is, so passing that folder is the whole change. A bundle is rewritten with every structured-data name it already had kept, ``masks`` replaced, and the two structured-data names derived from the masks -- ``outlines`` and ``ismanual`` -- brought up to date with it (see :func:`save_seg_bundle`); that is what the external curation tool did to the same files, less its stale outlines. A convert step would have been a second copy of every microscope field of view, and the curator would have had to remember which copy was the truth.
records.translation: दोनों के लिए उसी जगह संपादन सही है, इसीलिए कोई रूपांतरण चरण नहीं है। sibling सेट nested सेट से केवल इसमें भिन्न है कि उसका मास्क फ़ोल्डर कहाँ है, इसलिए वह फ़ोल्डर देना ही पूरा बदलाव है। बंडल को उसकी हर मौजूदा कुंजी बनाए रखते हुए दोबारा लिखा जाता है, ``masks`` बदला जाता है, और मास्क से निकली दो कुंजियाँ -- ``outlines`` और ``ismanual`` -- उसके साथ अद्यतन की जाती हैं (:func:`save_seg_bundle` देखें); बाहरी क्यूरेशन टूल ने भी इन्हीं फ़ाइलों के साथ यही किया था, बस उसकी पुरानी आउटलाइन के बिना। रूपांतरण चरण हर फ़ील्ड की दूसरी प्रति होता, और क्यूरेटर को याद रखना पड़ता कि कौन-सी प्रति सत्य है।

records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.invert_intensity#7
records.source: ``unsigned integers`` the dtype's own range, so a ``uint16`` field is ``65535 - value``. A 12-bit camera writing into ``uint16`` therefore comes back in the top sixteenth of the range; a display that stretches by percentiles puts that back where a reader can see it, and the array is still exactly invertible, which a data-range complement would not be across two fields of different brightness. ``signed integers`` ``iinfo.min + iinfo.max - value``, the same complement on the range the dtype actually spans. ``bool`` logical not. ``floating point`` the ARRAY'S OWN range, ``min + max - value``, because a float image has no dtype maximum worth speaking of. The complement of a range maps its ends onto each other, so a second call computes the same two ends and comes back to the original -- but NOT bit for bit: ``s - (s - x)`` rounds twice, and the round trip is out by up to one unit in the last place of ``s``. Measured on a 200x200 field over 0..65535: 0.002 in ``float32`` and 4e-12 in ``float64``, against an interval of one count. The round trip is EXACT for every integer and boolean dtype, which is every dtype a field is read in.

records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.invert_normalized#3
records.source: WHY NORMALISING FIRST IS THE POINT AND NOT A DETAIL. The Otsu threshold correction is a MULTIPLIER on an absolute level, so what it means depends on where the field's intensities sit. A dtype complement moves a 12-bit field (216..4095) up into 61440..65535, and a correction of 0.8 then asks for a cut below every pixel present while 1.3 asks for one above them all -- the dial becomes an on/off switch, which is the measurement recorded in :func:`invert_for_detection`. Normalising to the field's own range first puts EVERY field on the same 0..1 span before the multiplier is applied, so one correction value means the same thing on the next image.
records.context: Why normalising first is the point and not a detail. Normalising to the microscope field of view's own range first puts EVERY microscope field of view on the same 0..1 span before the multiplier is applied, so one correction value means the same thing on the next image.

records.source: WHAT IS GIVEN UP, said plainly: this is not exactly reversible on the original numbers the way the dtype complement was. records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.maxima_propagate_instances#1
records.source: Convert the field to float32, optionally blur it, and find centres with :func:`skimage.feature.peak_local_max`. Use those centres as markers for :func:`skimage.segmentation.watershed` on the negative blurred image. Distinct centres can split touching objects; noise can create extra centres, while smoothing or large centre spacing can remove real ones. No existing primary-object mask is accepted. This implementation has no CellProfiler propagation cost or distance/intensity weighting.
records.context: Convert the microscope field of view to float32, optionally blur it, and find centres with :func:`skimage.feature.peak_local_max`. Use those centres as markers for :func:`skimage.segmentation.watershed` on the negative blurred image. Distinct centres can split touching objects; noise can create extra centres, while smoothing or large centre spacing can remove real ones. No existing primary-object mask is accepted. This implementation has no CellProfiler propagation cost or distance/intensity weighting.
records.translation: फ़ील्ड को float32 में बदलें, वैकल्पिक रूप से धुंधला करें, और :func:`skimage.feature.peak_local_max` से केंद्र खोजें। उन केंद्रों को ऋणात्मक धुंधली छवि पर :func:`skimage.segmentation.watershed` के लिए मार्कर के रूप में उपयोग करें। अलग-अलग केंद्र सटे हुए ऑब्जेक्ट को विभाजित कर सकते हैं; शोर अतिरिक्त केंद्र बना सकता है, जबकि चिकनाई या बड़ा केंद्र अंतराल वास्तविक केंद्र हटा सकता है। कोई मौजूदा प्राथमिक-ऑब्जेक्ट मास्क स्वीकार नहीं किया जाता। इस कार्यान्वयन में CellProfiler की प्रसार लागत या दूरी/तीव्रता भार नहीं है।
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.source: Gaussian standard deviation in pixels; default 2.0. Positive values smooth both seed finding and growth; zero disables blur. Increasing it can suppress noise peaks or merge real peaks. Make Masks offers 0 to 50; the direct API also skips negative values.

records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.maxima_propagate_instances#3
records.source: ``seed_fraction`` first partitions the entire image by watershed, then retains pixels at or above ``stop_value`` times their basin's seed intensity. This is an intensity ratio, not a quantile. Adding a background offset changes the relative cut; equal measurements of bright and dim objects are not guaranteed. Trimming can leave disconnected pieces with the same label.
records.context: ``seed_fraction`` first partitions the entire image by watershed, then retains pixels at or above ``stop_value`` times their basin's seed intensity. Trimming can leave disconnected pieces with the same label.
records.translation: ``seed_fraction`` पहले पूरी छवि को watershed से विभाजित करता है, फिर उन पिक्सेल को रखता है जो अपने बेसिन की सीड तीव्रता के ``stop_value`` गुना पर या उससे ऊपर हैं। यह तीव्रता अनुपात है, क्वांटाइल नहीं। पृष्ठभूमि ऑफ़सेट जोड़ने से सापेक्ष कट बदलता है; चमकीले और मंद ऑब्जेक्ट के समान मापन की गारंटी नहीं है। छँटाई एक ही लेबल वाले असंबद्ध टुकड़े छोड़ सकती है।

records.translation: इनपुट तैयार करना कॉलर की ज़िम्मेदारी है: यह फ़ंक्शन तीव्रताओं को सामान्यीकृत नहीं करता, पृष्ठभूमि नहीं घटाता, और अँधेरे ऑब्जेक्ट को नहीं उलटता। परिमित 2-D मानों का उपयोग करें; NaNs और अनंत मान साफ़ नहीं किए जाते। Make Masks अपने चुने गए एन्हांसमेंट के बाद संसाधित फ़ील्ड या क्रॉप देता है। इसलिए निरपेक्ष स्तर और शिखर अनुपात उस तैयारी पर निर्भर करते हैं।

records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.normalise_filters#1
records.source: Accepts the list itself, one dict, ``(property, min, max)`` tuples, or the list written as JSON or as a Python literal (a settings file stores it as text). Every entry is checked here, once, so a typo in a property name fails when the list is read rather than on the hundredth field.
records.context: Accepts the list itself, one key-value mapping, ``(property, min, max)`` tuples, or the list written as JSON or as a Python literal (a settings file stores it as text). Every entry is checked here, once, so a typo in a property name fails when the list is read rather than on the hundredth field.
records.translation: स्वयं सूची, एक dict, ``(property, min, max)`` टपल, या JSON या Python लिटरल के रूप में लिखी सूची स्वीकार करता है (सेटिंग्स फ़ाइल इसे पाठ के रूप में संग्रहीत करती है)। हर प्रविष्टि यहीं एक बार जाँची जाती है, ताकि गुण नाम में टाइपो सौवें फ़ील्ड पर नहीं, बल्कि सूची पढ़ते समय ही विफल हो।
records.review_basis: written from the English (no current MT draft)

records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.normalise_filters#3
